key_insight: The paper shows that control theory, optimal transport, probabilistic inference, non-equilibrium thermodynamics, and machine learning can all be viewed through the shared lens of optimizing free-energy-like objectives under constraints.
engineering_relevance: This unifying perspective can help engineers transfer algorithms and intuition across reinforcement learning, variational inference, and generative modeling to design more principled learning systems.
method: Build a conceptual bridge across five fields with common variational and dynamical principles
Frame learning tasks as optimization of free-energy-like functionals
Illustrate applications in reinforcement learning, variational inference, and generative modeling
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a review and guided tour of theory-to-application links rather than a new experimental dataset or benchmark evaluation.
watch_item: Because it is a conceptual review, the unification may be elegant but still requires careful mapping of assumptions when applying ideas across domains.
paper_title: Bridging Control, Inference, Transport, and Thermodynamics: From Theory to Applications in Learning
